quests.instruction: Explain what has happened in this store, based only on what you can see. Start with what is on the floor.
quests.hint: Say what seems to have happened, then the evidence: what is on the floor and who is nearby.
quests.explanation: The learner reports an event with hedging ('seems to have collapsed') and supports it with visible clues.
quests.sceneText: Collapsed Display|shopper looking at the mess|empty display base|cans rolling across the floor
quests.sampleAnswer: A display of cans seems to have collapsed. The display base is empty, and cans are rolling across the floor toward the aisle while a shopper stands nearby, looking at them.
acceptedSynonyms: cans rolling,cans on the floor,rolling cans

quests.instruction: Report to a staff member what is on the floor and what has been put there to warn people.
quests.hint: Say what is on the floor first, then what warns people, then what a shopper is doing.
quests.explanation: A report describes the hazard, the warning, and the reaction of people around it, which is how someone would tell a manager.
quests.sceneText: Broken Jar|shattered jar with sauce spreading|yellow caution cone|shopper steering a cart around it
quests.sampleAnswer: A jar of sauce has broken on the floor, and the red sauce is spreading across the tiles. A yellow caution cone has been put next to it, and a shopper is steering a cart around it.
options: Shopper steering a cart around it
acceptedSynonyms: shopper with a cart,shopper steering,person avoiding the spill

quests.instruction: Explain what the problem is at the entrance and what people are doing about it.
quests.hint: Say what is wrong with the door, then what customers and the worker are doing.
quests.explanation: The learner explains a visible problem at an entrance and the responses of different people, in a short report.
quests.sceneText: Stuck Shop Door|customers waiting outside|door stuck half open|worker with a screwdriver
quests.sampleAnswer: The automatic door is stuck half open, so only one person can pass at a time. A few customers are waiting outside, and someone inside is working on the frame with a screwdriver.
acceptedSynonyms: worker with a screwdriver,person with a tool,man fixing the door

quests.instruction: Describe the two directions of movement and find the person who is going the wrong way.
quests.hint: Say which side people are using to go up and down, then who is going the wrong way.
quests.explanation: The learner describes two opposing flows and then one exception, which is a precise way to report movement in a crowd.
quests.sceneText: Busy Stairs|people going up the left side|people coming down the right side|person moving against the flow
quests.sampleAnswer: People are going up the left side of the stairs and coming down the right side. One person in a gray coat is pushing against the flow on the wrong side.
options: People going up the left side
People coming down the right side
acceptedSynonyms: people going up,people on the left,upward flow
people coming down,people on the right,downward flow
person against the flow,person in a gray coat,person going the wrong way

quests.instruction: Explain how the gate area works right now: who is moving and who is waiting. Start with the person who is moving through.
quests.hint: Say what people are doing, then what the gate light shows.
quests.explanation: The learner describes movement and waiting in the same scene, using visible clues (a red light) to explain why people wait.
quests.sceneText: Ticket Gates|line of people waiting|gate showing a red light|person tapping a card
quests.sampleAnswer: People are lining up to pass through the gates. One person is tapping a card on the reader, while the gate next to it shows a red light and several people are waiting.
acceptedSynonyms: red light,gate with a red light,closed gate
person tapping a card,person at the reader,person with a card

quests.instruction: Describe how people are using the escalator: who is walking and who is standing. Start with the people who are walking.
quests.hint: Give each group its own side of the picture before you add details.
quests.explanation: Two groups using the same escalator differently ('walking' versus 'standing') is a real pattern that the learner can describe with position words.
quests.sceneText: Escalator|people walking on the left|people standing on the right|suitcases beside the rail
quests.sampleAnswer: On the left, people are walking up the steps quickly. On the right, people are standing still, and a few suitcases are leaning beside the rail.

quests.instruction: Explain what is happening in the office: who is alone and who is working with others. Start with the person who is alone.
quests.hint: Say what the man is doing alone, then the woman, then the group.
quests.explanation: The learner contrasts solo work and group work in one office scene, using present progressive for each person.
quests.sceneText: Open Office|woman writing at a whiteboard|man on a video call|team gathered at a meeting table
quests.sampleAnswer: A man at his desk is on a video call with headphones on. A woman is writing on a whiteboard, and a team is gathered around a meeting table.
options: Team gathered at a meeting table
acceptedSynonyms: woman at the whiteboard,woman writing,whiteboard woman
man on a video call,man with headphones,man at his desk
team at the table,group at the table,people meeting

quests.instruction: Explain what is happening at reception. Start with the person who has just arrived.
quests.hint: Give each person one action and say who is doing it at the same time.
quests.explanation: Three actions happening at once ('signing in', 'handing over', 'answering') need different verbs and a linking phrase like 'at the same time'.
quests.sceneText: Office Reception|visitor signing in|courier handing over a package|woman answering the phone
quests.sampleAnswer: A visitor is signing in at the desk, and a courier is handing over a package. A woman behind the desk is answering the phone at the same time.
acceptedSynonyms: woman answering the phone,woman on the phone,receptionist

quests.instruction: Explain what is happening in the break room. Start with the person who is alone.
quests.hint: Describe one person alone, then the pair, then the line.
quests.explanation: The learner describes a small, everyday scene with three groups doing different things, each with a visible position.
quests.sceneText: Break Room|two people chatting by the fridge|man refilling coffee|line at the microwave
quests.sampleAnswer: A man is refilling his coffee at the machine, and two people are chatting by the fridge. A small line is waiting at the microwave.
options: Two people chatting by the fridge
acceptedSynonyms: man refilling coffee,man with coffee,man at the machine

quests.instruction: Explain the problem to the maintenance office over the phone.
quests.hint: Say what the problem is, where it is, and what is nearby.
quests.explanation: Explaining a problem to someone who cannot see it needs the problem, the place, and a nearby landmark.
quests.sceneText: Flickering Light|ladder leaning by the wall|person looking up|flickering ceiling light
quests.sampleAnswer: One of the ceiling lights in the corridor is flickering on and off. A person is looking up at it, and there's a ladder leaning against the wall nearby.

quests.instruction: Explain the problem to a colleague so they can fix it.
quests.hint: Say what is wrong with the handle, how it is attached now, and what else you can see.
quests.explanation: The learner explains a repair problem with what is loose, what has fallen, and what has been left as a note.
quests.sceneText: Broken Door Handle|screw on the floor|door handle hanging loose|handwritten note on the door
quests.sampleAnswer: The handle on this door is hanging loose from one screw. Another screw is on the floor, and a handwritten note is stuck to the door.
acceptedSynonyms: handwritten note,note on the door,paper note

quests.instruction: Explain the problem to the building manager.
quests.hint: Say what is open, what is moving because of it, and what else is affected.
quests.explanation: The learner explains a visible problem with a cause (the open window) and its effects (the curtain, the papers).
quests.sceneText: Stuck Window|window stuck open|curtain blowing inward|papers lifting off the desk
quests.sampleAnswer: A window is stuck open about ten centimeters and doesn't seem to close. The curtain is blowing inward, and some papers are lifting off the desk.
acceptedSynonyms: papers lifting,papers on the desk,loose papers

quests.instruction: Describe how the building changes from the first photo to the last. Focus on the middle stage.
quests.hint: Use 'in the first photo', 'in the second', and 'in the last'.
quests.explanation: Describing a change across photos teaches 'in the first ... in the second ... in the last', a common way to describe time.
quests.sceneText: Construction Photos|photo of the foundation|photo of the walls going up|photo of the finished roof
quests.sampleAnswer: In the first photo there's only a concrete foundation. In the second, the walls are going up, and in the last photo the roof is finished.
options: Photo of the walls going up
acceptedSynonyms: foundation photo,photo of the foundation,concrete base
walls going up,photo of the walls,second photo
finished roof,photo of the roof,last photo
quests.correctAnswer: Photo of the walls going up

quests.instruction: Describe how the scene changes from afternoon to night. Focus on the last stage.
quests.hint: Use 'at first', 'then', and 'finally' for the three changes.
quests.explanation: Sky color and lights are visible signs of time passing, so the learner describes a change without guessing the hour.
quests.sceneText: Evening Sequence|bright blue sky|orange sky over the roofs|city lights coming on
quests.sampleAnswer: At first, the sky is bright blue. Then it turns orange above the roofs, and finally the city lights come on.
acceptedSynonyms: orange sky,sunset sky,sky over the roofs

quests.instruction: Describe how the harbor changes as the water rises. Focus on the last stage.
quests.hint: Describe the starting state, the change, and then the final state.
quests.explanation: The learner describes a slow change in three stages with 'resting', 'creeping', and 'floating', three precise verbs for each stage.
quests.sceneText: Harbor Tide|boats resting on the sand|water creeping up the beach|boats floating at the dock
quests.sampleAnswer: At first, the boats are resting on the sand. Then the water creeps up the beach, and finally the boats are floating at the dock.
acceptedSynonyms: boats on the sand,resting boats,grounded boats
floating boats,boats at the dock,boats afloat

quests.instruction: Explain how far the assembly has got and what the man is doing.
quests.hint: Say what is done and what is not done yet, then what the man is doing.
quests.explanation: Describing a process in progress ('half assembled', 'still on the floor') shows the learner how to state stages and current action together.
quests.sceneText: Flat-Pack Shelf|half-assembled shelf|parts laid out on the floor|man holding an Allen key
quests.sampleAnswer: The shelf is half assembled: the sides are standing, but the back panel is still on the floor. A man is tightening a screw with an Allen key, and the rest of the parts are laid out beside him.
options: Parts laid out on the floor
acceptedSynonyms: parts on the floor,laid out parts,loose parts
man with an Allen key,man tightening a screw,man with a tool

quests.instruction: Explain the steps of the process you can see. Start with the part of the job that is already done.
quests.hint: Say what has been done (pinned), what is being done (marking), and what is in use.
quests.explanation: The learner describes three stages or tools at once, which is how someone would explain a visible repair job.
quests.sceneText: Hemming Trousers|woman marking with chalk|trousers pinned at the hem|tape measure on the table
quests.sampleAnswer: The trousers are pinned at the hem, and a tape measure is lying on the table. A woman is marking a line with chalk, so sewing is probably the next step.
acceptedSynonyms: woman marking,woman with chalk,woman drawing a line
tape measure,measuring tape,tape on the table

quests.instruction: Describe the stages of the process from raw to finished.
quests.hint: Use 'first', 'next to', and 'the oven door is open' to place each stage.
quests.explanation: The learner describes a process by its stages (raw dough, cooling cookies) and adds a detail (the open oven) that links them.
quests.sceneText: Baking Cookies|dough balls on a tray|cookies on a cooling rack|open oven
quests.sampleAnswer: First, there are balls of dough on a baking tray. Next to the oven, cookies are cooling on a rack, and the oven door is open.
acceptedSynonyms: cooling cookies,cookies on a rack,baked cookies

quests.instruction: Use 'seems' carefully: what might have happened at the table, and what is your evidence? Start with the clue that shows people left something behind.
quests.hint: Start with 'It seems...' and then name two clues.
quests.explanation: Hedging ('it seems') plus evidence is an honest way to report a guess without claiming something that cannot be seen.
quests.sceneText: Table Left Behind|plates of half-eaten food|two empty cups|jackets left on the chairs
quests.sampleAnswer: It seems the people at this table have stepped away for a moment. Their jackets are still on the chairs, and the plates are half eaten.
acceptedSynonyms: jackets on the chairs,coats on the chairs,left jackets

quests.instruction: Describe what seems to have happened with the weather, using evidence. Start with the clearest clue on the ground.
quests.hint: Say what seems to have happened, then list three visible clues.
quests.explanation: The learner uses 'seems' plus three clues (wet pavement, shaken umbrellas, moving clouds), which makes a guess more convincing.
quests.sceneText: After the Rain|wet pavement with puddles|people shaking umbrellas|dark clouds moving away
quests.sampleAnswer: It seems like it has just rained: the pavement is wet with puddles, people are shaking their umbrellas, and the clouds are moving away.

quests.instruction: What seems to be happening here? Say what you can see that supports your idea. Start with the clue that shows the work is partly done.
quests.hint: Say what you think is happening, then what supports it.
quests.explanation: The learner reports a guess ('someone is cleaning') and supports it with the clean pane, the dirty pane, and the tools.
quests.sceneText: Window Cleaning|bucket with soapy water|one clean window pane|squeegee on the sill
quests.sampleAnswer: It seems someone is cleaning the windows. One pane is clean and shiny, but the next one is still dirty, and a bucket of soapy water and a squeegee are on the sill.

quests.instruction: Explain what the woman is trying to do and what is making it difficult.
quests.hint: Say what she is trying to do, then what makes it hard, then what is out of reach.
quests.explanation: 'Is trying to' describes a visible attempt, and 'out of reach' explains why it is hard.
quests.sceneText: High Shelf|stool across the room|woman stretching for a jar|jar on the top shelf
quests.sampleAnswer: The woman is trying to reach a jar on the top shelf. She's stretching up on her toes, but the jar is still out of reach, and a stool is standing across the room.
acceptedSynonyms: woman stretching,woman reaching,woman on her toes
jar on the top shelf,jar,high jar

quests.instruction: Start with the object the man is trying to open, then say what he is using.
quests.hint: Say what he is trying to do, then how, then what tool is available.
quests.explanation: 'Trying to open' and 'gripping with both hands' describe an attempt and the effort that goes into it.
quests.sceneText: Stuck Jar|rubber glove on the counter|man gripping the lid|jar with a tight lid
quests.sampleAnswer: The man is trying to open a jar with a tight lid. He's gripping the lid with both hands, and a rubber glove is lying on the counter.
acceptedSynonyms: man gripping,man with both hands,man opening
jar with a tight lid,stuck jar,jar

quests.instruction: Explain what the girl is trying to do and what makes it hard.
quests.hint: Say what she is doing, then what is out of reach, then who is not watching.
quests.explanation: 'Is on tiptoe' and 'out of reach' explain what she is trying to do, and 'with his back turned' adds a detail of the scene.
quests.sceneText: Sweet Shop Counter|girl on tiptoe at the counter|jar of sweets out of reach|man with his back turned
quests.sampleAnswer: The girl is on tiptoe at the counter, trying to reach a jar of sweets. The jar is on a high shelf, and a man behind the counter has his back turned.
options: Girl on tiptoe at the counter
Jar of sweets out of reach
acceptedSynonyms: girl on tiptoe,girl at the counter,girl reaching
jar of sweets,sweet jar,jar out of reach
man with his back turned,man behind the counter,man turned away
quests.correctAnswer: Girl on tiptoe at the counter

quests.instruction: Explain what is happening on the belt and how the parts connect.
quests.hint: Follow the objects along the line from start to end.
quests.explanation: The learner follows an object through a process ('moving', 'filling', 'catching'), so each part of the line connects to the next.
quests.sceneText: Bottle Line|bottles moving along the belt|machine filling the bottles|crate at the end of the belt
quests.sampleAnswer: Empty bottles are moving along the belt toward the filling machine. The machine is filling each bottle, and at the end of the belt, a crate is catching the filled ones.
options: Crate at the end of the belt
acceptedSynonyms: crate,crate at the end,box of bottles

quests.instruction: Explain how the water moves from the roof to the ground. End with where the water finally goes.
quests.hint: Follow the water from the gutter to the barrel to the ground.
quests.explanation: Following the path of water ('from the gutter', 'into the barrel', 'onto the ground') is a way to describe cause and effect that can be seen.
quests.sceneText: Downspout|rain pouring from the gutter|barrel overflowing|puddle spreading across the ground
quests.sampleAnswer: Rain is running off the roof into the gutter and pouring out of the downspout. It's filling a barrel that is already overflowing, and a puddle is spreading across the ground.

quests.instruction: Describe how the two children's movements are connected. Start with the child who is going down.
quests.hint: Say what each child is doing, then what connects them.
quests.explanation: The learner describes two linked movements ('rising' and 'dropping') and the point that connects them, which is a simple example of cause and effect.
quests.sceneText: Seesaw|girl rising on one end|boy dropping on the other end|pivot in the middle
quests.sampleAnswer: A girl is rising on one end of the seesaw while a boy on the other end is going down. They move together around the pivot in the middle.
options: Boy dropping on the other end
acceptedSynonyms: girl rising,girl going up,girl on one end
boy dropping,boy going down,boy on the other end
quests.correctAnswer: Boy dropping on the other end

quests.instruction: Give a dynamic report in six or seven sentences: what is happening, who is doing what, how it is organized, and what is at the far end. Make the person who is checking a list your focus.
quests.hint: Start with the whole event, then the movement, then the details, then the end point.
quests.explanation: Level 140 completes the dynamic block: a report of a moving scene in six or seven sentences, with actions, organization, and an end point.
quests.sceneText: Fire Drill|people walking in lines|person with a clipboard|sign at the meeting point
quests.sampleAnswer: This is a fire drill. A large group of people is walking out of the building in two lines. Near the front, a person is looking at a clipboard while people pass. Most people are carrying nothing, but a few are holding phones. At the far end of the yard, a sign marks the meeting point, and people are gathering under it. The doors behind them are open, and nobody is running.
acceptedSynonyms: person with a clipboard,person with a list,clipboard

quests.instruction: Give a dynamic report in six or seven sentences: what is wrong, where, who is doing what, and what is being done.
quests.hint: Start with the main problem, then the people, then what they are doing, then the surroundings.
quests.explanation: The learner reports a moving scene with a clear structure: problem, place, people, actions, and surroundings.
quests.sceneText: Flooded Street|car stuck in the water|people wading across|sandbags at a doorway
quests.sampleAnswer: A car is stuck in deep water in the middle of a flooded street. The water reaches the bottom of its doors. On the pavement, two people are wading across with their bags held up, and a man is placing sandbags in front of a doorway. Further back, other cars have stopped, and nobody is driving. The shops on both sides look closed.
acceptedSynonyms: car in the water,stuck car,car stuck
sandbags,sandbags at a doorway,bags at the door

quests.instruction: Give a dynamic report in six or seven sentences and finish with the people moving the set.
quests.hint: Start with the whole stage, then the curtain, the lights, and end with the people.
quests.explanation: The final task describes a busy scene with moving people and equipment, and finishes with the action that matters most.
quests.sceneText: Stage Between Scenes|curtain half open|lights on a rail|people moving a wooden set
quests.sampleAnswer: This is a stage between scenes. The curtain is half open, so you can see the back of the stage. Lights hang on a rail above, and several are pointing at the floor. Four people in dark clothes are carrying a wooden set piece across the stage, and one is holding the end to guide it. A ladder is leaning against the side wall.
acceptedSynonyms: lights on a rail,stage lights,overhead lights
people moving a set,people carrying a set piece,stage hands
